images.after: The fake brand deal: how creator accounts get taken over
images.title: How a fake brand deal takes a channel
images.alt: Flow of the fake sponsorship attack: forged offer, software download link, file run, session cookies sent to attacker, channel sold or rebranded.
images.caption: Stealing the session cookie skips your password and MFA, which is why the no-unknown-files rule matters.

items.label: Forged collaboration offer
items.text: Sent to the channel's business email, posing as a real company

items.label: Download link
items.text: A "software download" page, by email or inside a PDF on Google Drive

items.label: The file runs
items.text: It sends the browser's session cookies to the attacker

items.label: Account taken over
items.text: The attacker acts as you without logging in, so MFA never gets a say

items.label: Channel resold
items.text: Hijacked channels are sold or rebranded to stream crypto scams

images.after: This week: email, domain and money accounts
images.title: This week's account checks
images.alt: Checklist covering email recovery details, forwarding rules, a private admin address, registrar lock, auto-renew, payout details and updates.
images.caption: Start with email and your domain, since whoever controls them can reset or redirect almost everything else.

items: Recovery email and phone on your main email are yours and current
No forwarding rules, filters or old third-party apps you didn't set up
Unpublished admin address as the login for registrar, host, payments
MFA on at the registrar and DNS provider; domain shows as locked
Auto-renew on, with a current card on file
MFA on payment, ad, affiliate and list accounts; payouts unchanged
Automatic updates on for your OS, browser, phone, CMS and plugins

images.title: Sharing a login vs inviting a collaborator
images.alt: Comparison of sharing your password with an editor or assistant against inviting them under their own account with the lowest role and MFA.
images.caption: Most platforms have roles or team seats, so a shared password is rarely the only way to get help.

columns.label: Shared password
points: Their laptop becomes part of your security
Access stays until you change the password

columns.label: Own account, own role
points: Lowest role that lets them do the job
MFA required on their side too
Removed the same day they stop working with you
